evidence.dominant_driver: NYT-reported US proposal to extend the China trade truce by six months ahead of the Trump-Xi summit; later contemporaneous reporting says no extension is confirmed.

market_expectations.expected_value: Markets already expected the Trump-Xi summit to focus on extending the November trade truce.
market_expectations.distribution_notes: Proposal is constructive but not an agreement.

absorption.reason: US equities were already sharply higher and Nasdaq leadership was strong; the headline reinforced an existing US-China/AI risk-on narrative.

observations.interpretation: Risk-on context confirms de-escalation, but much of the move predates the headline.

evidence.decision_notes: Residual forecast from 16:45 UTC, not original reaction. M2 learning: 1h directional confidence 5-6 is ACTIONABLE REDUCE_OR_AVOID while 1h low-confidence MIXED is ACTIONABLE KEEP_NEUTRAL, supporting a neutral residual 1h call.

immediate.rationale: The headline is over two hours old and equities had already rallied strongly; residual impulse is limited.

next_session.rationale: A confirmed extension or constructive Trump-Xi follow-through would lower tariff risk into the next session.

15m.rationale: The headline is over two hours old and equities had already rallied strongly; residual impulse is limited.

1h.rationale: The US proposal is supportive, but Reuters reports no extension was confirmed, limiting directional edge.

4h.rationale: Trade de-escalation helps risk assets, but the market is extended and confirmation is absent.

next_session.rationale: A confirmed extension or constructive Trump-Xi follow-through would lower tariff risk into the next session.

predictions.mechanism: A longer US-China truce lowers tariff, supply-chain and policy uncertainty; technology has high direct exposure.
predictions.invalidation: Chinese rejection, US walk-back, renewed tariff threats, or a broad risk-off reversal would invalidate the next-session upside view.
predictions.counter_case: The proposal may already be priced and China may seek a longer arrangement; without agreement, the headline can fade.
